solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Where software or floppy can be loaded (3,5,3,4)

indicatorNotes.floppy: something floppy has lost its firm shape, so the letters lose their order

annotation.surface: A computer-shop question about where a program or a floppy disk can be installed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads floppy as the old computer disk and loaded as installed software; in fact floppy scrambles the letters and loaded means drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for drunk, and someone the worse for wear after a night out is in exactly that state.

entries.clue: Half-hearted fast about to be broken by papa (5)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, facing the other way, so DIET runs backwards
indicatorNotes.to be broken by: something broken is split open, and P goes into the gap

blocks.note: to fast is to go on a strict diet
Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A half-hearted attempt at fasting that is about to be broken by Dad.
annotation.walkthrough: Fast looks like speed but is the noun for going without food, and the surface's 'broken' fast is a false lead to breakfast.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym by extension: tepid water is lukewarm, and a lukewarm response is a half-hearted one.

entries.clue: Just be all over the shop with tequila (9)

indicatorNotes.all over the shop: British idiom for scattered everywhere and disorganised, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A warning that a night on the tequila leaves you all over the place.
annotation.walkthrough: Just reads as the adverb 'only', starting a sentence; it is the adjective meaning fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a just ruling is a fair one, treating each side evenly.

entries.clue: It’s my fault husband has left rings (4)

indicatorNotes.has left: 'has left' in the sense of walked out: the husband departs and takes his letter H with him

annotation.surface: A spouse owning up that her husband walked out and took the rings with him.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a marriage breaking up, with rings as wedding rings; they are hoops, and the husband is the single letter H.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the exclamation blurted out on making a slip, standing in for the admission of blame.

entries.clue: Gluttony bound to hinder fellow having sex (7)

indicatorNotes.to hinder: to hinder is to get in the way, so F lodges in the middle of SURE and blocks it

blocks.note: bound to happen = sure to happen

annotation.surface: Greed tied up with a man's appetite for sex.
annotation.walkthrough: Bound looks like tied up but means certain, as in bound to win.
annotation.definitionFit: Overindulgence: a surfeit is an excess, above all of food and drink, which is where gluttony leads.

entries.clue: Unkempt sort in XS jumper given sack (7)

indicatorNotes.given: given something means it is handed over and added on, so BAG follows

blocks.note: an extra-small jumper: a tiny insect that leaps

annotation.surface: A scruffy person in an extra-small jumper who has just been fired.
annotation.walkthrough: XS jumper looks like a small-size sweater (jumper is British for sweater) and given the sack looks like being fired; the jumper is a tiny insect that leaps.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British insult: a fleabag is a dirty, shabby person, as if crawling with vermin.

entries.clue: Type of company dealing with a conservative (9)

blocks.note: per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative party

annotation.surface: A firm whose dealings are with a Conservative politician.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a business relationship; the company is a theatre troupe.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a repertory company keeps a stock of plays and performs them in rotation.

entries.clue: Want to remove dead electrical connection (5)

indicatorNotes.to remove: 'to remove' means take something away, here the D at the front

blocks.note: a dearth is a want, a lack

annotation.surface: Wishing to take out a dead wire in a circuit.
annotation.walkthrough: Want looks like a verb, wishing; it is the noun meaning lack.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term: what Americans call a ground wire the British call an earth, the connection that carries fault current away.

entries.clue: Republican lie missed by Democratic party (9)

indicatorNotes.missed by: something missed by a person is absent from them, so the D goes missing

annotation.surface: A Republican falsehood that the Democratic Party fails to notice.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'Democratic party' together as the US political party; the definition is party alone, a social gathering.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a formal party, such as the one after a wedding.

entries.clue: More stout left for pick-up by pint-puller? (7)

indicatorNotes.for pick-up by: to be picked up by something is to be taken aboard it, so L is carried inside PUMPER

blocks.note: a barman pulls pints by pumping beer, so is a pumper

annotation.surface: A barman fetching a glass of stout that a customer left to be collected.
annotation.walkthrough: Stout is set up as the beer a pint-puller serves; it is the adjective meaning fat. The question mark flags PUMPER as a made-up word for a barman.
annotation.definitionFit: Stout here is the adjective meaning fat, so more stout is fatter, the comparative the answer also gives.

entries.clue: Crime PI worked on for a scientist? (7)

indicatorNotes.worked on: clay that is worked on is kneaded into a new shape, and so are the letters

annotation.surface: A private detective working a case on behalf of a scientist.
annotation.walkthrough: PI is a private investigator on the surface and only letters in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, hence the question mark: an empiric relies on observation and experiment, the method of a scientist.

entries.clue: Make old-fashioned dish and two egg starters (4)

indicatorNotes.starters: a starter is what comes first, so take the first letter of each word before it

blocks.note: first letters of Dish And Two Egg

annotation.surface: A retro recipe: one old-fashioned dish and a couple of eggs to start.
annotation.walkthrough: Starters looks like the first course of a meal, fitting dish and egg; it tells you to take the first letter of each of the four words.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain verb sense: a thing that shows its age marks itself as belonging to the past, which makes it seem old-fashioned.

entries.clue: An arm and a leg, pelvis or body? (10)

blocks.note: arms and legs are limbs, an old sense of members
the hip is the pelvic region

annotation.surface: A list of body parts ending with a question about the whole body.
annotation.walkthrough: An arm and a leg also suggests a high price; here it is simply two limbs. Body is meant as a group of people, like a governing body.
annotation.definitionFit: A second sense of body: a club or society taken as a whole group of people, all those who belong to it.

entries.clue: Home ground a short distance into Derby? (7)

indicatorNotes.into: one thing going into another ends up inside it, so A BIT sits within HAT

blocks.note: a derby is a bowler hat

annotation.surface: A football supporter's home stadium a short way into Derby, the English city.
annotation.walkthrough: Derby reads as the English city or a local match; the question mark marks it as an example of a hat, the bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym from natural history: the ground an animal naturally lives on is its home ground.

entries.clue: Hospital with new antigens for fast-tracking (9)

indicatorNotes.new: new means made afresh, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A hospital rushing new antigen tests through approval.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is medical news; new is only an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: speeding a thing along is the same as fast-tracking it.

entries.clue: Will group put back unexciting books? (9)

indicatorNotes.put back: put back in the sense of turned backwards, so SET runs in reverse

blocks.note: NT is the standard abbreviation for the second half of the Bible, a collection of books

annotation.surface: Asking whether a reading group will shelve its dull books again.
annotation.walkthrough: Will reads as the helping verb; it is the legal document.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal phrase: the document is formally a 'last will and testament', and the second word alone carries the same meaning.

entries.clue: In hearing, condemn EasyJet’s top Italian fare (7)

indicatorNotes.In hearing: what is in hearing is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by sound
indicatorNotes.top: the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: condemn = knock (criticise), plus the first letter of EasyJet; said together they give the anglicised pronunciation

annotation.surface: A passenger in earshot of the crew rubbishing the food served on an EasyJet flight.
annotation.walkthrough: EasyJet is a British budget airline; only its first letter is used. The sound match relies on the anglicised 'nocky' pronunciation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: these potato dumplings are a classic dish of Italian cooking.

entries.clue: Hit scorer freshly-arranged for Sonic Youth? (9)

indicatorNotes.freshly-arranged: arranged afresh, as a song is re-arranged, so the letters take a new order

annotation.surface: A hit song rearranged for the American rock band Sonic Youth.
annotation.walkthrough: Sonic Youth is a noisy American rock band, fitting the puzzle's music theme; the question mark asks you to read the name literally.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading of the band name: a youth who makes sound, such as a boy singing in a church choir.

entries.clue: Around New Year, small boy’s covering for head (7)

indicatorNotes.Around: one thing placed around another encloses it, so S and SON enclose TET

blocks.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival, placed inside

annotation.surface: A little boy wearing a hat around New Year.
annotation.walkthrough: The New Year is not Western: Tet is the lunar New Year in Vietnam, and it sits between S and SON.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the broad-brimmed cowboy hat is one kind of covering for the head.

entries.clue: Not any affluent nurses head for Windy City (7)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold something close, so RICH holds W inside it
indicatorNotes.head for: the head of a word is its front, its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Windy, placed inside after the R

annotation.surface: No wealthy nurses are heading for Chicago, the Windy City.
annotation.walkthrough: Windy City is Chicago's nickname, but the definition is City alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cathedral city in Norfolk, eastern England.

entries.clue: Record or song by Blue (3,4)

blocks.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

annotation.surface: A record or a single by the British boy band Blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue is a British pop group, keeping up the band theme; here it is the mood. Record is a verb, not a disc.
annotation.definitionFit: Studio jargon: putting a track on tape for the first time is the phrasal verb in the answer.

entries.clue: Get jammy US extract (phosphorus-free) (4,3)

indicatorNotes.free: '-free' means without, as in sugar-free, so the phosphorus is left out

blocks.note: to pluck out is to extract
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus, the letter removed

annotation.surface: Getting lucky with an American fruit extract that contains no phosphorus.
annotation.walkthrough: Jammy is British slang for lucky, and US flags that the answer is the American way of saying it.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use, flagged by US: the American phrase for striking it lucky, which the British call being jammy.

entries.clue: It’s a farce travelling around a foreign region (4,6)

indicatorNotes.travelling around: things travelling around move from place to place, and so do the letters

blocks.note: the last letter of the fodder

annotation.surface: A traveller complaining that touring an overseas region is a shambles.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one tourist's grumble; all ten letters of 'It's a farce' and 'a' are shuffled.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a region of the African continent, abroad from the setter's British viewpoint.

entries.clue: Wait on minister to deliver work for Deal (5)

blocks.note: what a waiter does at table
the legal sense, handing over a writ or summons
to be employed by a master or a country
as a verb, to hand out portions of food or cards

annotation.surface: A waiter expecting a church minister to hand over a job in Deal, a town in Kent.
annotation.walkthrough: Every phrase is a meaning of SERVE, five in a row. Deal is capitalised to look like the Kent seaside town.
annotation.definitionFit: Every sense is a plain synonym: you serve diners, someone's needs, a writ, an employer, and portions of food.

entries.clue: Support member of nobility on radio (4)

indicatorNotes.on radio: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by sound

blocks.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

annotation.surface: A radio phone-in where a lord backs a cause.
annotation.walkthrough: Support is a noun here, a pillar, not the verb 'back'.
annotation.definitionFit: An architectural sense: a solid pillar that holds up an arch or bridge span.

entries.clue: Mature beef no good with side of nuggets (5)

indicatorNotes.no: no good means without the good, so the G is dropped
indicatorNotes.side of: an edge of the word, here its last letter

blocks.note: a beef is a gripe, a complaint

annotation.surface: Aged beef that turns out no good, served with some nuggets.
annotation.walkthrough: Mature and beef suggest a butcher's hanging meat; a beef is slang for a complaint.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: fruit and cheese both grow ready over time, which is to mature.

entries.clue: Soprano bursting into so-so Come Together (4)

indicatorNotes.bursting into: to burst into a room is to enter it forcefully, so S forces its way inside MEH

annotation.surface: A soprano breaking into a lacklustre cover of the Beatles song Come Together.
annotation.walkthrough: Come Together is a Beatles song, capitalised for the music theme; here it just means fit together.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: gears engage when their teeth come together, and ideas can do the same.

entries.clue: Serial rewritten by one for The National (7)

indicatorNotes.rewritten: a text rewritten is set down again differently, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: A serial rewritten by one member of the American rock band The National.
annotation.walkthrough: The National is an American indie band; the definition is national as a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: National as a noun means a citizen of a country, and the answer names a citizen of one particular country.

entries.clue: Dance record by a certain Stone (3-4)

indicatorNotes.by: by in the sense of beside, so the record stands next to ONE ST

blocks.note: st = stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: A dance record by one of the Rolling Stones.
annotation.walkthrough: Stone looks like a Rolling Stone; it is the unit of weight, abbreviated ST.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a quick ballroom dance of the early twentieth century.

entries.clue: Flighty type of big pale horse unseated one (5,5,5)

indicatorNotes.unseated: a rider unseated is thrown off, so the I is thrown out of HEROIN

annotation.surface: A skittish kind of big pale horse that has thrown its rider.
annotation.walkthrough: Flighty, horse and unseated all point to a nervy racehorse; flighty means able to fly, and horse is slang for heroin.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful synonym: a flighty type is one that flies, and this large wading bird of Florida does.
